key_insight: An EHR-integrated generative AI tool improved VTE risk detection sensitivity compared with checklist-based and clinician judgment workflows, though specificity was lower than the checklist approach.
clinical_relevance: The study suggests AI may help identify more at-risk hospitalized patients for thromboprophylaxis, but it should support—not replace—clinical judgment and chart review.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine.
Compared iHGR and clinician-selected order sets against physician-adjudicated reference standard.
Sampled 500 adult inpatient admissions from 758 eligible cases, balanced by site and workflow period.
evidence_signal: Across 500 admissions, iHGR achieved 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity versus the reference standard, with performance compared directly to two real-world order set workflows.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting the challenge of capturing unstructured clinical information and the need for careful implementation.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
